relations.note: Developed Purāṇic genealogy names Vajrāṅga as Tāraka’s father.
Developed Purāṇic genealogy names Varāṅgī as Tāraka’s mother.
Later summaries loosely place Tāraka among Diti’s descendants.
Tārakākṣa is one of Tāraka’s three sons and Tripura rulers.
Vidyunmālin is one of Tāraka’s three sons and Tripura rulers.
Kamalākṣa is one of Tāraka’s three sons and Tripura rulers.

relations.myth: Tāraka receives protective power after austerities
relations.note: Brahmā grants Tāraka protection from gods, asuras, and rākṣasas.

relations.myth: Brahmā reveals how Tāraka can be defeated
relations.note: Brahmā tells the gods that a newly produced divine child can circumvent the boon.

relations.myth: Tāraka conquers and subordinates the gods
relations.note: Developed accounts depict Tāraka defeating or displacing Indra before the divine counterattack.

relations.myth: Agni carries the power producing Tāraka’s killer
relations.note: Agni carries Śiva’s generative energy, indirectly enabling the birth of Tāraka’s killer.

relations.myth: Gaṅgā bears the power producing Tāraka’s killer
relations.note: Gaṅgā carries the embryo or energy that becomes Skanda.

relations.myth: Śiva supplies the power producing Tāraka’s killer
relations.note: Tāraka’s immunity necessitates Śiva’s son, and Śiva supplies the generative power.

relations.myth: Pārvatī becomes mother of Tāraka’s destined killer
relations.note: The classical synthesis makes Pārvatī mother of the son destined to kill Tāraka.

relations.myth: Kāma awakens Śiva for the Tāraka crisis
relations.note: The gods send Kāma to awaken Śiva’s desire so a son can defeat Tāraka.

relations.myth: Rati laments Kāma during the Tāraka crisis
relations.note: Rati mourns Kāma’s burning within the causal chain leading to Tāraka’s defeat.

relations.myth: Skanda leads the divine army against Tāraka
relations.note: Tāraka battles the youthful commander and, in developed accounts, wounds him and his peacock.

relations.myth: Skanda kills Tāraka with the divine spear
relations.note: Skanda kills Tāraka, normally by piercing his chest or heart with the śakti.

relations.myth: Viṣṇu joins the gods’ campaign against Tāraka
relations.note: Recension-dependent Purāṇic accounts have Tāraka withstand or counter Viṣṇu before Skanda attacks.

relations.myth: The Kṛttikās nurse Tāraka’s destined killer
relations.note: The Kṛttikās nurse or collectively mother Skanda, indirectly enabling Tāraka’s defeat.

relations.myth: Skanda defeats Tāraka and Mahiṣa among the asuras
relations.note: Tāraka and Mahiṣa appear as separate asuras defeated by Skanda; no kinship is stated.
Tamil tradition makes Tāraka a brother of Śūrapadma.

relations.myth: The asura brothers wage war against Murukaṉ
relations.note: Tāraka serves within the allied asura family and campaign headed by Śūrapadma.
Tamil tradition presents Siṃhamukha as another brother of Tāraka.

relations.myth: The asura brothers wage war against Murukaṉ
relations.note: Tāraka and Siṃhamukha belong to the same allied asura campaign.

relations.myth: Gaṇeśa assists Skanda in preliminary battles
relations.note: Some late vernacular narratives place Gaṇeśa among forces assisting against Tāraka’s campaign.

relations.myth: Kṛṣṇa urges Skanda to strike Tāraka
relations.note: A late recension has Kṛṣṇa urge hesitant Skanda to use the śakti against Tāraka.
